page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-48-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the c4n server family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs and 180.0 GB of system memory, which provides an allocation of 3.75 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include any GPU resources, making it entirely dependent on its CPU capabilities for processing tasks.

The storage configuration presents a specific tradeoff: while the basic description references 8 local SSDs and the storage type is listed as nvme ssd, the local storage size is formally specified as None. Additionally, the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which must be factored into networking and connectivity planning.

With a dedicated CPU allocation and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio of 3.75 GB per core, this server is designed for compute-intensive workloads that require consistent CPU performance without GPU acceleration. Appropriate workloads include web serving, batch processing, and distributed compute tasks. The qualitative cost efficiency of this hardware profile is defined by its high density of dedicated vCPUs relative to its memory allocation.
